decisions.question: Stop-rule scope (branch -stop-, finding F1, plan 6.4/D-6): should the one-pass 'trivial and content unchanged' stop end every Improve child, or only the document stages, with a measured two-clean-pass confirmation kept for implement-step and end-of-work code reviews?

options.label: A. One pass for every Improve child (as built: 60018152, 3b9ca9c9)
options.effect: Document stages: the study's 21 passes become 15 (replay stops spec 7/8, test-strategy 2/5, plan 3/4, step-plan 1/1, test-spec 2/3; measured by replay). Code reviews: the 7 implement-step reviews of the live Salesforce run (5+3+1+1+1+1+1 = 13 passes) become 9, -4 passes (projected 4 to 8 min at the study's 2.0 min per pass).
options.cost: No extra code; the runtime change is already built.
options.risk: Cuts the one late code defect on record: implement child adfd6e3b took P1 edit, P2 'No material finding', P3 found that Apex == on strings ignores case (every black piece read as white, black castling lost), P4 and P5 clean; gate 2 stops it at P2. The study measured only five document stages and says not to extend to code reviews. n=1 find in 2 multi-pass code reviews.

options.label: B. One pass for the 7 `improve: always` document stages; implement and carry-forward stop on a first pass that is unchanged (main's rule) and, after any edit, need two consecutive passes that are trivial AND measured-unchanged (new vendored-only gate value 3)
options.effect: Document-stage saving unchanged (same replay, 21 -> 15 passes). Code reviews unchanged from today: adfd6e3b stays 5 passes (P3 find kept), ed863ab3 stays 3, the other five end at P1. Zero added cost against main.
options.cost: About 15 lines in the vendored runtime `done` (a clean-pass count and an 'edited earlier' flag), `improve_start_contract` picks the gate from STAGE_SPEC[stage].improve, two replay cases, and a stage-kind variant of the one-pass wording the stop branch wrote for every stage (the contract's exit_condition, the handoff 'Review passes' sentence, improve/SKILL.md 'Exit rule', review-policy.md, the S-10 carve-out). Forgoes the 4 passes option A would save.
options.risk: A second repurposed value in the vendored fork. Upstream (0.8.3) the field is a count, so the published plugin would read 3 as three trivial reviews; Improve contracts run only on the improve card's bundled runtime (`_start_improve` uses child['skill']['runtime_cli']), so there is no live exposure today, but it is the same skew class as gate 2 (finding F5, Backchain converge).

options.label: C. Keep main's rule everywhere (two trivial labels, or one when the first pass changed nothing); drop the stop-rule branch
options.effect: No document-stage saving: the replay's 6 of 21 passes (about 4 min net per run) are not taken.
options.cost: Discards the built runtime change and the S-10 carve-out work.
options.risk: Three polish edits per five document stages keep forcing two more passes each (study: spec P6, test-strategy P3, plan P2).

decisions.recommendation: B. Gate 2 (one trivial, unchanged pass) for spec, test-strategy, plan, step-plan, test-spec, system-test-author and release-plan; gate 3 for implement and carry-forward. Have the script record per pass whether the one-pass rule would have stopped (IMP-11 passes.md) and re-decide option A when 10 step reviews with at least 3 edits exist. This narrows the owner's 2026-10-16 'one unchanged pass' decision to the stages the study measured; it does not touch the 2026-09-26 unchanged-first-pass rule (2be7906b), which B keeps for code reviews.
decisions.rationale: The study that justifies the rule covers five document stages (system-test-author and release-plan are documents of the same kind, unmeasured) and its own limits say not to extend it to code. The only multi-pass code reviews on record show the extension zone is where a real late defect sat. B costs nothing against today (code reviews keep main's pass counts) and keeps every measured saving, so it passes the owner's decision order (a material quality difference trumps; near-identical quality then fewest tokens, then time) without a trade. Option A's extra 4 passes are a projection from one Grok run; a missed code defect would likely be caught later by the test stage (not measured), which is why this is a call for the owner, not a rule.
evidence: docs/shiploop-improve-stop-rule-journal-2026-10-16.md (branch -stop-): 21 passes, 8 material, 10 with no change; three polish edits reset the streak; replay stops 7/2/3/1/2.

Pass counts per implement child in the same run (counted from reviews/): adfd6e3b 5, ed863ab3 3 (P1 edit, P2 and P3 'Finding: none material'), e4cc9c04 1, cab5e8d4 1, bf9ed336 1, be354b65 1, 09af30a7 1 = 13; under gate 2 the first two stop at P2 (computed by me from the review text).

decisions.question: Stop-rule P1s F2 (installed-skill-invocation is red on the branch and not selected by the quick tier) and F3 (a non-Git in-place run can never start its first Improve review): fix both, or constrain F3 by refusing non-Git runs at init? Which is KISS?

options.label: A. Fix both. F2: two one-line catalog mappings plus `git init` in the two failing fixtures. F3: measure a non-Git workspace through a throwaway bare repository inside the runtime's `_workspace_tree`.
options.effect: F2: a change under skills/improve/runtime/until-loop/ selects until-loop-vendor and installed-skill-invocation (today neither: `suite_catalog.targeted` returns 13 ids without them for until_loop_ephemeral.py). F3: the unchanged-content rule works the same outside Git; I proved the measurement in a scratch probe (`git init --bare` in a temp dir, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, temp index, `write-tree`: equal tree id twice, different id after an edit).
options.cost: About 12 lines in `_workspace_tree`, one runtime test, the 'must be a Git worktree' sentences in ADAPTER.md, runtime-ephemeral.md and the change note. No fixture changes beyond the two.
options.risk: A big non-Git tree with no ignore rules hashes slowly each pass; the existing 60 s timeout still refuses start with the existing message. The route is exceptional (SKILL.md: an explicit in-place/non-Git run).

options.label: B. Fix F2; constrain F3: `init` refuses a non-Git --repo and names `workspace start` or `git init` first
options.effect: The failure appears at launch instead of at the first Improve review.
options.cost: Measured by a logging patch in a scratch clone across all 87 ShipLoop suites: 103 `init` calls on non-Git directories in 12 suites (keepalive 59, skill-calls 14, cross-run 13, consumer-delivery-cli 4, no-model-launch 4, auth-readiness 2, rehydration 2, navigator-contract, status-display, progress, navigator-v4, narrative). Each fixture needs a `git init`, and four documents lose the direct-entry route.
options.risk: Removes a documented capability: SKILL.md 'An explicitly selected in-place/non-Git run may instead use the direct entry', and `shiploop_knowledge_home.commit` still says 'not a checkout: nothing to commit, as before'. Refuses a run that would otherwise work for a long document.

options.label: C. Fix F2; document F3 (not a normal run, KISS)
options.effect: Nothing changes in code.
options.cost: Zero.
options.risk: A real stuck state: `_improve_stage_start` prints the refusal to stderr and leaves the stage pending; the pending packet then names `improve-start --restart-stopped`, which calls `_start_improve` and fails the same way. A model asked to proceed with no way out is the hang owner rule 13 forbids.

options.label: D. Degrade the gate to `required_trivial_reviews 1` for non-Git (the runtime's own error text suggests it)
options.effect: The run proceeds.
options.cost: `_progress` in shiploop_standalone_improve.py requires gate 2 and `last_pass_changed_tree is False`; the terminal-packet check does too: three places change, plus tests.
options.risk: Re-admits a label-only exit that the study's must_not_reintroduce forbids.

decisions.recommendation: A. F2 is two mapping lines in test/suite_catalog.py `_PREFIX_SUITE_IDS` (key skills/improve/runtime/until-loop/ -> until-loop-vendor, installed-skill-invocation) plus `git init` in the two fixtures. F3 is the throwaway-bare-repository measurement: same rule outside Git, no gate value, importer or fixture change.
decisions.rationale: KISS is the smallest change that keeps a documented route working. Every other Git-dependent gate already degrades outside Git (commit returns Committed('', []), capture_base is unavailable, improve_changes.review_changes returns None), so refusing only Improve is the inconsistent choice. Option B costs 9 or more fixtures and a capability; C leaves a stuck run; D re-opens the label-only exit. Option A is not a version or a fallback rule: the same measurement, another way to compute the tree.
evidence: Ran test/installed-skill-invocation.test.py on main + stop + packets + loop in a scratch clone: 2 failures, 'required_trivial_reviews 2 (unchanged content) needs a content tree the runtime can measure: the workspace must be a Git worktree ... otherwise use required_trivial_reviews 1' (SP/eff2/r2/installed-skill-merged.txt).

python3 -I probe of test/suite_catalog.py: targeted(['skills/improve/runtime/until-loop/scripts/until_loop_ephemeral.py']) = 13 ids, no 'until-loop-vendor', no 'installed-skill-invocation'; PROVENANCE.json selects until-loop-vendor only.
skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_navigator.py `_improve_stage_start` (prints 'ShipLoop could not start the Improve review', leaves the stage pending) and `_improve_restart` (same `_start_improve`).
Scratch probe SP/eff2/r2/ng/tree.sh: tree id 972b5b8f... twice for equal content, 092bf420... after an edit, in a directory where `git rev-parse` fails.
skills/shiploop/SKILL.md lines 211-225 (explicit in-place/non-Git entry); skills/shiploop/scripts/shiploop_knowledge_home.py `commit` ('not a checkout: nothing to commit, as before').
Logging patch of shiploop_protocol.py in a scratch clone, SP/eff2/r2/probe-logs/*.log (non-Git init census: 103 calls, 12 of 87 suites).
decisions.what_would_change_it: The owner stating that non-Git in-place runs are not a supported route (then B, and delete the documented route in four files), or a large real non-Git tree whose hash exceeds the 60 s timeout.
decisions.confirm_by: Add to test/improve-runtime.test.py: a gate-2 start in a non-Git temp directory is accepted, an edit changes the tree, an unchanged trivial pass completes; add a catalog test that targeted() of the runtime script names until-loop-vendor and installed-skill-invocation; rerun installed-skill-invocation (12 tests, 2 red today).

decisions.question: Callback placement: keep the owner rule and the index pointer above the callback (the callback moves from line 2 to line 4, as built in f3f6a6bc), or put them after it?

options.label: A. As built: header, owner rule, pointer, callback (callback begins at char 469 on line 4 at a 163-char run dir)
options.effect: A lost-context reader meets the pointer first, as the owner asked ('the first line of each packet should say ...'). Visible in every observed cut: `| head -N` had N 8 to 60 over the 20 complete calls, 14 to 50 on the 7 producer prints.
options.cost: About 424 chars above the callback at 163; two command cards say 'the line after the header' (shiploop-next.md, shiploop-complete.md) and are now false.
options.risk: A warm model reads a conditional line it does not need every packet; the plan's gate 'warm next calls not above control' measures that.

options.label: B. Callback on line 2; owner rule and pointer after it
options.effect: Restores the pinned position (rehydration, delegation, improve-schedule, navigator-contract, planning-handoff).
options.cost: A three-line swap and the pins move back.
options.risk: Contradicts the owner's words; the artifact shows no visibility gain from line 2.

options.label: C. A, with the block bounded by a test and rewritten by plan 5.5 (Recovery command first; owner rule moves to the Fill site if D-9 takes it)
options.effect: The top block is at most 5 lines and the 'Callback for this stage' label stays within the first 8 lines and 1,500 chars at 83 and 163 chars, for every stage, route and packet kind.
options.cost: One head-position test and the two card edits.
options.risk: None found beyond A.

decisions.recommendation: C. Keep the lines above the callback (the owner's wording decides), bound the block with a position test, and repair the two stale cards by naming the label ('the line starting Callback for this stage') instead of a line number. Do not spend a battery arm on the order.
decisions.rationale: Where the model looks first is not the callback line: it opens things by label (`grep -A60 'Current stage guidance'`, 'Argument:', 'Exit when') and cuts its own prints at N of 8 or more lines, so line 2 versus line 4 changes nothing it sees; it followed 0 of 103 listed pointers. What changes behaviour is a command it can run, which plan 5.5 supplies. The cost of the placement is bytes above the block, which matters only through the head budget (R4).
evidence: SP/eff2/findings-cross.json X-1: 20 of 20 complete calls piped through head, N 8 to 60 (median 20), producer prints N = 50,30,30,40,14,30,25; X-9: grep by label, 0 of 103 listed pointers opened.

options.effect: Reorder alone, 83-char dir (line simulation on the merged render, projected): the loop block ends near char 18,900 and the cut falls on Recovery tail, Pause, the Knowledge sentence and HEAD_END. 163-char dir: the cut drops the end of the Result sentence and the contract note plus chrome; the 652-char start command survives. decisions.question: Merge order and release grouping for -packets-, -loop- and -stop- (plan Step 1.0, D-16, D-23): which together, which separately, which tests gate each, and does the vendored until-loop change wait for an upstream release?

options.label: A. Plan as written: one integration branch, merge stop -> packets -> loop, reconcile, one release
options.effect: One verification run and one refresh.
options.cost: Holds the only change with a measured time gain (the stop rule) behind the packets and loop reconciliation and their owner decisions (R3, R4, D-26, the unknown-skill host line).
options.risk: The named base `feat/shiploop-eff-release-ca2c6e` no longer exists: it shipped as 2.5.0 (da9e2e75). The plan also defers any release of the packets pointer until Step 3.3 retargets it.

options.label: B. Integrate all three on a new branch off main in the order stop, packets, loop (any order merges clean); release the stop rule on its own, the packets and loop with the later text waves
options.effect: The owner's checkout E2E run sees all three; the stop rule's planning-time effect (replay 21 -> 15 passes, about 4 min net) is not held for the head work.
options.cost: Two releases and two preflights (each shiploop release needs a LEARNINGS entry or a No-E2E-Round trailer). Reconciliation list is longer than Step 1.0 states: symbols-guard exemption for the loop Work lines (68 failures), head order and ceilings (packet-recut 2, step-packets 1), a skill-calls.jsonl row in the context-index map (rehydration).
options.risk: Version skew at gate 2 between the published until-loop plugin and the vendored fork until upstream adopts the change (affects Backchain converge only, opt-in; default `one` pass uses gate 0).

options.label: C. Release each branch separately
options.effect: Smallest blast radius per release.
options.cost: Three releases; packets alone is red (packet-recut 20,005 > 20,000; rehydration 'skill-calls.jsonl'), so it needs fixes before it can ship by itself.
options.risk: Three host refreshes for text changes that share one head budget.

options.label: D. Wait for the upstream until-loop release before shipping the stop rule
options.effect: No fork of the vendored runtime.
options.cost: Blocks on the owner's upstream go and the marketplace pin (D-5).
options.risk: Delays the largest measured planning-time lever; the fork has precedent (ADAPTER.md is already a recorded adaptation) and a hash test.

decisions.recommendation: B. New integration branch feat/shiploop-eff-tr1-<hex6> off main da9e2e75 (revise D-23). Merge stop first (after R1, R2 and the S-10 text), then packets, then loop, each a merge commit with G-SUITES between; reconcile in the loop merge commit. Release the stop rule separately and do not wait for upstream: PROVENANCE.json records the adaptation and test/until-loop-vendor.test.py enforces it; open the upstream change in parallel because a re-vendor must carry it.
decisions.rationale: The three branches are independent: they merge textually clean in either order and their red sets are disjoint (stop: installed-skill-invocation only; packets: packet-recut by 5 chars and rehydration; loop: green alone). Only stop has a measured time gain; packets and loop add head bytes (+610 and +555 chars at 83) for owner-asked wording and need the R3/R4/D-26 decisions plus a Claude slice for the Skill-tool host line. D-16 already says the vendored change ships separately.
evidence: Scratch clone SP/eff2/rel-ac9e47 (main da9e2e75 + stop + packets + loop, all `git merge --no-ff` exit 0, also clean in the order packets, loop, stop).

All 87 ShipLoop suites on the merged tree (groups shiploop-1/2/3, SP/eff2/r2/probe-out-shiploop-*/receipt.json): exactly four red: shiploop-packet-recut 2 failures (20,484; 22,166), shiploop-packet-completeness 68, shiploop-step-packets 1 (20,460), shiploop-rehydration 1 (MasterIndexTests entry 'skill-calls.jsonl', hook x packets). `quick --changed-from origin/main` selected 68 suites and shows the same four red (62 of 68 done when written; SP/eff2/r5/quick-all3/receipt.json).

decisions.question: Skill-call hook: OpenCode (and any non-Claude host) started from a bound Claude shell is still gated. What is the minimal robust rule? Also D-24 (Claude-only accepted) and the P2 limits (judged from disk config; calls before binding).

options.label: A. Add OpenCode's own marker to NESTED_NON_CLAUDE and pin it with a table test over keepalive.HOSTS
options.effect: OPENCODE in the environment turns the gate off, like CODEX_THREAD_ID, CODEX_SANDBOX and CURSOR_PLUGIN_ROOT today. Red/green proved in a scratch clone: with OPENCODE=1 `skill_gate` returns enforce True on main; after the one-element change all 30 skill-call tests pass.
options.cost: One tuple element and one test row; a test that every host in keepalive.HOSTS other than claude has a nested marker (fails when a host is added without one).
options.risk: Another nested host with an unknown marker (Cursor's CLI agent) is not measured.

options.label: B. 'Exactly Claude's marker set': enforce only when no other host family's variables are present
options.effect: Would catch unknown hosts.
options.cost: A prefix rule.
options.risk: Not implementable: Claude's own shell here carries CODEX_COMPANION_SESSION_ID and CODEX_COMPANION_TRANSCRIPT_PATH (set by the Codex plugin), so a CODEX_ prefix would switch the gate off for Claude users who have that plugin.

options.label: C. Walk the process ancestry (ps) and enforce only if the nearest host binary is Claude
options.effect: Robust to unknown markers.
options.cost: A subprocess per gate and platform-specific ps parsing.
options.risk: More machinery than the gap (an OpenCode started from a bound Claude shell on the same run) is worth; not KISS.

options.label: D. Require positive proof that the session recorded any Skill call since binding

options.label: D-26 keep both lines on the bound Improve packet (as built, shiploop_navigator.improve_packet via _owner_lines)
options.effect: Every Improve packet carries the owner rule and the recovery pointer: +344 chars on a packet of 2.0 to 2.9 KB (+12 to 17%).
options.cost: The pointer names context-index.md today (0 opens in 16 breaks); plan 5.5 retargets it.
options.risk: Contradicts improve-packet-minimal (2026-10-11: 'no rules, goal, references, recovery prose').

options.label: D-26 drop both lines from the bound Improve packet; keep a pointer only on the pending or stopped Improve packet, which already carries a literal command
options.effect: The Improve packet stays at its floor: header, the two steps, Keepalive marker, status, narrative. A cleared parent still has the run directory in the literal `complete` command.
options.cost: One deletion at the improve_packet call site and the OwnerLinesTests rows for Improve.
options.risk: If the owner meant 'each packet' to include Improve (2026-10-16), this is the opposite of what they asked; reversible by one line.

options.label: D-4 two-step: `improve-pass` composes and prints the literal runtime `done` and `complete` commands; the model runs them
options.effect: Hooks and permission prompts see each command; the model's typed tail shrinks (plan 6.3 target 4.3 -> 1.5 KB).
options.cost: The model still chooses when to run `done`, so the skill-call refusal can arrive after the loop is terminal (IMP-2).
options.risk: A model that types `done` by hand never calls improve-pass.

options.label: D-4 single verb: ShipLoop runs `done` in its own subprocess
options.effect: One command; the refusal could precede `done`.
options.cost: A command leaves the host shell tool; the runtime `done` averages 7.4 s over 29 calls in the live run (plan figure, not re-measured), hidden inside one ShipLoop call.
options.risk: Breaks the owner's hooks-must-see-every-command rule (2026-10-11) by intent: hooks, permission prompts and sandboxes would no longer see `done`.

decisions.recommendation: D-26: drop both lines from the bound Improve packet and keep the Recovery pointer only where the packet is already a recovery packet (pending, stopped, unbound). D-4: no; keep two-step, and make the skill-call refusal's named exit work when the child is already terminal by naming `improve-start --restart-stopped` (the route exists for a first-pass-unchanged child), submitting that exit through the real gate in a test.
decisions.rationale: The Improve rule is explicit and later restated ('any time we run improve, it's really just calling the improve skill and then ... done'); the Improve packet was followed exactly 4 of 4 in the artifact and the pointer adds nothing a literal callback lacks. The owner-rule line's style content reaches Improve through the opening and handoff recipe (plan 8.3), so dropping it from the packet loses no style direction. The 2026-10-16 'each packet' words most plausibly meant producer packets, but only the owner can say, so one line of confirmation is needed. For D-4 the hooks rule decides by intent, and the real flaw IMP-2 found is the ordering of the check, which is fixed by a working named exit rather than by moving `done` out of the host shell.
